category_overview: The six tools form three layers. Gong is conversation and revenue intelligence that sits on top of the CRM; HubSpot's Breeze Assistant and Agent Hub are AI native to the CRM itself; LinkedIn's Sales Navigator and Hiring Assistant monetise LinkedIn's member graph for prospecting and recruiting; Google Ads AI (AI Max, Performance Max, Ask Advisor) and Meta Advantage+ are opaque optimisation suites inside the two dominant ad platforms. Gong, HubSpot and Sales Navigator overlap on account research and outreach drafting and are increasingly wired together (Gong exposes MCP servers to HubSpot and Microsoft 365 Copilot; Sales Navigator Advanced Plus syncs into HubSpot, Salesforce, Dynamics and Oracle). Google and Meta compete for the same performance budgets and are converging on "give us a URL and a budget" automation while removing manual controls (DSA and language targeting at Google; placement exclusions and legacy ASC/AAC APIs at Meta). Enterprises usually standardise on one CRM-native assistant (HubSpot or Salesforce Einstein), add Gong for enterprise sales coaching and forecasting, licence LinkedIn seats to sales and talent teams, and treat Google and Meta AI as unavoidable defaults that marketers must learn to steer rather than tools they choose.

tools.name: Gong AI
tools.vendor: Gong.io Inc. The brief's guess "Gong" is correct; Gong markets the platform as the "Gong Revenue AI OS" with modules Gong Engage, Gong Forecast, Gong Enable, Gong Agents and Gong Assistant.
tools.what_it_is: Gong records and transcribes sales calls, meetings and emails, then uses AI to summarise conversations, flag deal risk, coach reps and forecast revenue. It lives in its own web and mobile app (app.gong.io) and is surfaced inside Salesforce, HubSpot, Slack, Teams and Zoom; since February 2026 it also exposes MCP servers so Microsoft 365 Copilot, Salesforce Agentforce and HubSpot agents can query Gong data.
key_capabilities: Call and meeting capture, transcription and AI summaries across Zoom, Teams, Google Meet and telephony
Gong Assistant: conversational Q&A grounded in recorded customer conversations (launched Feb 2026)
Gong Forecast: AI deal-risk scoring and pipeline forecasting
Gong Engage: sequences, dialer and AI-drafted follow-ups
Gong Enable: AI Call Reviewer scorecards, AI Trainer role-play and Initiative Tracking
Account Console and Account Boards for renewal-risk and expansion signals; Gong Agents automate CRM edits and follow-ups
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Single enterprise contract (no self-serve tier). Gong's security page states "Your data is never used to train generative AI models"; data is hosted on AWS in segregated environments with encryption, MFA, role-based access and audit logging. Admin controls: redaction, deny lists, consent management in 70+ languages, retention and deletion policies (retention up to three years or contract length). Trust Center lists SOC 2 Type II (2026), ISO 27001:2022, 27017, 27018, 27701, ISO 42001 (AI management), PCI DSS SAQ-D, CSA STAR, TX-RAMP Level 2 and EU/Swiss/UK Data Privacy Framework; HIPAA controls are mapped inside the SOC 2 audit (Gong is not a covered entity). No FedRAMP. Gong help docs say an admin can choose an EU data centre, whereas a Dec 2025 third-party DPA review claimed US-only storage, so confirm residency contractually. SSO via identity and provisioning integrations.
tools.licensing_pricing: No published list prices. Pricing is per-user licences plus a platform fee that scales with user count; quotes come from a sales form by team size. Third-party estimates (Docket, May 2026): Foundation about US$1,400-1,600 per user per year, full bundle (Foundation + Engage + Forecast) about US$2,880-3,000 per user per year, platform fee US$5,000-50,000 per year, implementation US$15,000-65,000, typically 2-3 year terms. Not bundled with any suite.
tools.integrations: Salesforce, HubSpot CRM, Microsoft Dynamics 365; Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Google Meet; Slack; Snowflake and BI tools; LinkedIn Sales Navigator, ZoomInfo, G2, Gainsight, Chili Piper, Zapier; Microsoft 365 Copilot and other MCP clients; 250+ partners in the Gong Collective.
tools.recent_developments: Feb 25 2026 "Mission Andromeda" release: Gong Enable, Gong Assistant, Account Console/Boards and MCP interoperability with Copilot, Agentforce and HubSpot. Dec 2025: named Leader in Gartner Magic Quadrant for Revenue Action Orchestration. 2026 SOC 2 Type II and ISO 42001 added to Trust Center. VentureBeat reports about US$300M ARR and 5,000+ customers. Platform now branded "Revenue AI OS" (not a rename of Gong itself).
tools.best_fit_departments: 28 Sales - Enterprise & Key Accounts (Core): strongest fit for call summaries, account research and opportunity planning. 30 Sales Operations & Revenue Operations (Advanced): good for pipeline hygiene and forecast insight, but Docket notes 40% of Gong customers also pay for Clari, so treat forecasting fit as partial.
tools.training_notes: Learners must master call-recording consent and regional recording law, tracker and redaction configuration, critical reading of deal warnings and forecast categories, prompting Gong Assistant and checking answers against transcripts, and CRM hygiene so AI insights stay accurate. Core 6-8 hours for sellers; Advanced 12-16 hours for RevOps admins covering trackers, Forecast and MCP governance.
tools.caveats: Transcription accuracy degrades with accents and non-native English; Docket finds Gong Assistant weak on deeper queries; Smart Trackers need ongoing maintenance; API lacks bulk export; expensive with multi-year terms and early-termination penalties; EU data centre disables some dialer features (personal-number calling, Foundation mobile dialer); pricing opaque.

tools.name: HubSpot AI
tools.vendor: HubSpot, Inc. Brief guess correct. Marketed as Breeze Assistant, Agent Hub, Agent Builder and Smart CRM; the "Breeze" umbrella brand (launched INBOUND 2024) is being retired in the Fall 2026 Spotlight.
tools.what_it_is: AI embedded throughout HubSpot's customer platform (Marketing, Sales, Service, Content and Revenue Hubs). Breeze Assistant is an in-app chat assistant; Agent Hub runs prebuilt autonomous agents (Customer, Prospecting, Data, Content, Campaign, Nurture, Revenue, Knowledge Base, Deal Progression); Agent Builder creates custom agents in natural language. HubSpot data is also reachable from ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot and Gemini via connectors and the HubSpot MCP Server.
key_capabilities: Prospecting Agent monitors buying signals and drafts personalised outreach (US$1 per recommended lead)
Customer Agent resolves chat, email, voice and social enquiries (US$0.50 per resolved conversation; HubSpot claims 65% resolution)
Breeze Assistant drafts emails and content, summarises records and preps meetings
Campaign, Content and Nurture agents build campaign plans, write brand-aligned content and personalise sequences
Smart CRM enrichment and buyer intent (formerly Breeze Intelligence) plus Data Agent
Context Home scores data completeness so agents share one context
tools.enterprise_data_handling: All tiers: the "AI Model Training" toggle is ON by default so HubSpot may use account data to improve its own models; Super Admins can turn it off (forward-looking only), accounts with Sensitive Data enabled are auto-opted out, and opting out does not remove features. Third-party models (Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, Google Gemini, Perplexity Sonar per the model cards) run under "Model Zero Data Retention" and "No Customer Data Used For Third Party Model Training"; PII redaction available for AI Features. Admins control which data AI can access in the Access tab. Trust Center: SOC 2 Type II (scope includes Breeze and regional data centres), SOC 1 (June 2026), SOC 3, independent HIPAA attestation (2025), GDPR and EU Cloud Code of Conduct Level 2, EU data centre for residency, SSO (Okta), 2FA and passkeys. No FedRAMP; ISO 27001 not stated on the opened trust page.
tools.licensing_pricing: Sales Hub (USD, per seat/month): Starter shown at US$7 with US$20 as the regular monthly price; Professional US$90 annual / US$100 monthly plus US$1,500 onboarding; Enterprise US$150 plus US$3,500 onboarding. Marketing Hub: Starter US$7-20 per seat; Professional US$800-890 per month (annual vs monthly) including 3 core seats plus US$3,000 onboarding; Enterprise from US$3,600 per month including 5 seats plus US$7,000 onboarding. HubSpot Credits included 500/3,000/5,000 per tier, extra US$0.01 per credit, reset monthly. Agent Hub included from Starter; Customer and Prospecting agents Pro/Enterprise only, outcome-priced since 14 Apr 2026 with 28-day trial. Not bundled with any suite.
tools.integrations: Native Smart CRM; connectors for ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot and Gemini; HubSpot MCP Server; Breeze Assistant connectors to Gong, G2 and Asana; LinkedIn Sales Navigator Advanced Plus sync; Google Ads and Meta ad accounts via Marketing Hub; Zapier.
tools.recent_developments: Sep 2025: Breeze Copilot renamed Breeze Assistant. 14 Apr 2026: outcome-based pricing for Customer and Prospecting agents. Jul 2026: Agent Hub and Agent Builder public beta (replacing Breeze Agents and Breeze Studio). Sep 2026: conference renamed from INBOUND to UNBOUND; Fall Spotlight retires the Breeze brand, adds Campaign, Content, Nurture and Revenue agents, Context Home and HubSpot AEO. Jun 2026: first SOC 1 report.
tools.best_fit_departments: 29 Sales - SMB & Inside Sales (Core): excellent fit (Prospecting Agent, Assistant, Sales Hub sequences). 32 Digital & Performance Marketing (Advanced): good for campaign planning, nurture and reporting, but ad-auction optimisation is shallower than native Google or Meta tooling.
tools.training_notes: Master credit budgeting and agent monitoring in Agent Hub, AI access and model-training settings, writing the knowledge content agents depend on, editing generic drafts, and connector/MCP permission scoping. Core 6-10 hours for sales users; Advanced 12-16 hours for marketing ops and admins.
tools.caveats: Credits do not roll over; agent quality depends on CRM data completeness; default opt-in to HubSpot model training surprises buyers; mandatory onboarding fees at Pro/Enterprise; many agents are public beta and change fast; repeated renames make internal documentation stale quickly.

tools.name: LinkedIn Recruiter AI
tools.vendor: LinkedIn Corporation (a Microsoft subsidiary), LinkedIn Talent Solutions. Brief guess correct. There is no SKU called "Recruiter AI": the capabilities are marketed as Hiring Assistant (an agent add-on) plus AI-Assisted Search and AI-Assisted Messages inside LinkedIn Recruiter.
tools.what_it_is: AI inside the LinkedIn Recruiter web product that automates role intake, sourcing across LinkedIn and the ATS, applicant screening, personalised InMail drafting and candidate pre-screening. Hiring Assistant is an agent bought as an add-on to Recruiter Corporate or Recruiter Professional Services Plus; it also surfaces in Microsoft Teams for hiring-manager feedback.
key_capabilities: Intake conversation builds a sourcing strategy beyond keywords and filters
Runs dozens of searches across LinkedIn and connected ATS data to rank candidates
Screens thousands of applicants and explains fit
AI-Assisted Messages draft personalised outreach (LinkedIn claims 44-55% higher acceptance)
Voice or text pre-screening of interested candidates (median 6 minutes in Hiring Assistant 2)
Microsoft Teams app, AI Follow-Ups and AI Applicant Targeting (Feb 2026 drop)
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Enterprise contract only. LinkedIn's SOC 2 and ISO 27001/27018 certifications cover Talent Solutions, with reports in its Smart Trust Center. LinkedIn cites its Responsible AI Principles and describes Hiring Assistant as "compliant by design". Microsoft's self-attested app page for the Hiring Assistant Teams app (developer update Dec 2025) says data is stored in the United States, retained under 30 days after termination and not passed to sub-processors, but answers "No" to SOC 2, SOC 3, ISO 27001 and FedRAMP for that app and does not integrate Entra ID SSO. Candidate data stays within LinkedIn and connected ATSs; no statement about training on customer data appears on the opened official pages.
tools.licensing_pricing: Contact sales. Recruiter pricing varies by organisation size and seat count; Hiring Assistant is a separately priced add-on requiring Recruiter Corporate or RPS+ seats (not Recruiter Lite). Herohunt (Oct 2026) cites a UK public rate card of GBP 1,575-2,079 per year for the add-on with monthly candidate-capacity tiers. Hiring Assistant 2 is a free automatic upgrade for existing English-language customers from November 2026. Not bundled with Microsoft 365.
tools.integrations: Major ATSs via LinkedIn Integrations (Greenhouse, Lever, SmartRecruiters, Zoho Recruit and Tracker cited for HA2 evaluation); Microsoft Teams; LinkedIn Jobs; connected apps for verified work portfolios.
tools.recent_developments: Hiring Assistant general availability Sep 2025. Feb 2026 quarterly drop: Teams collaboration, AI Follow-Ups, AI Applicant Targeting, Verified Applicant Spotlight. 29 Sep 2026: Hiring Assistant 2 announced with advanced reasoning, memory, verified identity and employer signals, ATS applicant evaluation and voice pre-screening, rolling out Nov 2026; LinkedIn says 20,000+ companies use its agentic hiring tools. Now available in seven languages.
tools.best_fit_departments: 12 Talent Acquisition (Advanced): strong fit for sourcing, screening and intake-driven job requirements. Interview-question design is outside its scope and is better served by a general assistant.
tools.training_notes: Master intake prompting, bias review (memory inherits prior hiring patterns), candidate-communication compliance (EU instant outreach is disabled), AI-hiring regulation such as NYC Local Law 144 and EU AI Act high-risk duties, and ATS sync hygiene. Advanced 12-16 hours.
tools.caveats: English-first with regional limits; cannot source outside LinkedIn and connected ATSs; performance metrics are LinkedIn self-reported; the add-on requires full Recruiter seats and unused capacity is forfeited; the Teams app lacks Entra SSO and product-level SOC 2 per Microsoft's attestation page; pricing opaque outside the UK rate card.

tools.name: LinkedIn Sales Navigator AI
tools.vendor: LinkedIn Corporation (Microsoft), LinkedIn Sales Solutions. Brief guess correct. AI features are marketed as Account IQ, Lead IQ, Message Assist, AI-Assisted Search, Buyer Intent and Sales Assistant (beta).
tools.what_it_is: A prospecting platform over LinkedIn's 1B+ member graph that adds generative summaries of accounts and leads, AI-drafted InMail and an agent that recommends daily leads and warm introduction paths. It lives in the Sales Navigator web and mobile app and, on Advanced Plus, is embedded in Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics 365, HubSpot Smart CRM and Oracle Sales.
key_capabilities: Account IQ one-click company briefs (priorities, financials, hiring and leadership signals) refreshed every 30-90 days
Lead IQ person briefs for meeting preparation
Message Assist AI InMail drafts (public beta, English, capped at 50 per month)
Sales Assistant (beta) delivers daily leads, explains fit, picks the warmest path in and drafts intro requests
Buyer Intent scoring from 180+ signals; TeamLink and relationship maps
AI-assisted and conversational search across 40+ filters
tools.enterprise_data_handling: LinkedIn's SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001/27018 certifications cover Sales Solutions. Features use "advanced AI models from LinkedIn, Microsoft, and OpenAI" (Azure OpenAI); ZoomInfo's Aug 2026 review reports LinkedIn's statement that user data is not used to train OpenAI or Azure OpenAI models. LinkedIn positions the AI as a co-pilot where "the seller always retains complete control". Advanced and Advanced Plus add Admin Center seat management, usage reporting and centralised billing; Advanced Plus adds CRM sync. No data-residency, HIPAA or FedRAMP statements found; Core is an individual subscription without admin controls.
tools.licensing_pricing: Core US$119.99 per month or US$1,079.88 per year; Advanced US$159.99 per month or US$1,799.88 per year (also priced in AUD, CAD, EUR, GBP); Advanced Plus is custom-priced via sales (ZoomInfo cites a 10+ seat minimum). The compare page lists Account IQ and Lead IQ on Core and Advanced, Message Assist on Advanced and Advanced Plus only. Not bundled with Microsoft 365 or Dynamics licences.
tools.integrations: Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics 365, HubSpot Smart CRM, Oracle Sales (CRM sync and embedded profiles on Advanced Plus; Oracle integration launched Oct 2025); Gong; Smart Links; Outlook. No public API and partner programme closed to new applicants.
tools.recent_developments: May 2025: Sales Assistant launched in beta (Snowflake, Thomson Reuters, Grant Thornton named). Oct 2025: Oracle Sales integration. 2026: progressive rollout of Sales Assistant and conversational search (June 2026 coverage), Message Assist public beta, Account IQ availability widened across plans by Aug 2026. No rename; still marketed as Sales Navigator.
tools.best_fit_departments: 34 Business Development & Partnerships (Core): strong fit for partner discovery, warm-path relationship mapping and first-touch outreach. Proposal drafting is not covered and needs a general assistant or CRM tool.
tools.training_notes: Master ICP and saved-search design, verifying AI briefs (Account IQ needs 200+ employee companies and excludes government and education), InMail etiquette and the 50-message cap, CRM sync field mapping, and GDPR/ePrivacy rules for outreach. Core 6-8 hours.
tools.caveats: Several AI features are beta and English-only; recipients are not told drafts are AI-written; no email or phone export; intent signals limited to LinkedIn's ecosystem; summaries can be weeks old; InMail credits cannot be purchased; Core plan excludes team administration.

tools.name: Google Ads AI
tools.vendor: Google LLC (Alphabet). Brief guess correct. Not a single SKU: the handbook label covers AI Max for Search, Performance Max, Demand Gen, Smart Bidding, Asset Studio generative tools (Gemini, Nano Banana Pro, Veo, Omni) and the Ads Advisor agent, which Google Marketing Live 2026 folded into a unified "Ask Advisor".
tools.what_it_is: Generative and predictive AI built into the Google Ads web console, Google Ads Editor and the Google Ads API. It broadens keyword matching, writes ad text from landing pages, allocates budget across Search, Shopping, YouTube, Display, Discover, Gmail and Maps, generates images and video, and through Ask Advisor answers natural-language questions and applies account changes after advertiser approval.
key_capabilities: AI Max for Search: search-term matching, text customisation and final URL expansion (Google claims 7-14% more conversions at similar CPA/ROAS)
Performance Max cross-channel bidding with channel reporting, negative keywords and asset experiments (Oct 2026)
Smart Bidding (tCPA/tROAS), journey-aware bidding and the Qualified Future Conversions metric
Asset Studio: Gemini copy, Nano Banana Pro images, Veo video, Omni on-brand video, Adobe Creative Cloud link
Ask Advisor agent spanning Google Ads, Analytics, Merchant Center and Marketing Platform; fixes policy issues and builds campaigns with consent
Gemini-powered dashboards and natural-language insights
tools.enterprise_data_handling: Governed by the Google Ads Data Processing Terms: data may be processed "in any country in which Google or its Subprocessors maintain facilities", Google commits to maintain ISO 27001 certification, gives 30 days' notice of new subprocessors and grants audit rights under EU law. business.safety.google lists ISO 27001 covering Google Ads and SOC 1 Type 2 for AdWords; SOC 2/3 are listed for Cloud and Workspace rather than Ads. AI Max writes assets from your landing pages and existing ads; the FAQ contains no separate privacy statement or opt-out from Google improving its systems. Admin control is via manager accounts and Google Workspace identity; no HIPAA or FedRAMP coverage for Ads. These terms apply to all advertisers (there is no enterprise tier).
tools.licensing_pricing: No licence or subscription: Google states "no flat fees or monthly subscriptions", pricing is a real-time auction on CPC, CPM, CPV or CPL with advertiser-set average daily or campaign total budgets (daily spend may reach 2x but not exceed the monthly limit). All AI features are included in media spend. Not part of Google Workspace.
tools.integrations: Google Analytics 4 and 360, Merchant Center, YouTube, Google Marketing Platform, Google Ads API and Editor, Adobe Creative Cloud (Asset Studio), HubSpot and other CRM ad connectors.
tools.recent_developments: Nov 2025: Ads Advisor and Analytics Advisor agents (English accounts, Dec rollout). Dec 2025: Nano Banana Pro image model in Ads. Mar 2026: Veo video generation. Apr 2026: Dynamic Search Ads upgrade to AI Max (auto-upgrades Sep 2026, DSA sunset moved to Feb 2027). 20 May 2026 GML: AI Max out of beta, Ask Advisor, Qualified Future Conversions, Asset Studio updates. Sep 2026: manual language targeting removed. Oct 2026: PMax asset experiments and channel prioritisation. PMax reached 4M advertisers (AdExchanger).
tools.best_fit_departments: 32 Digital & Performance Marketing (Advanced): direct fit for campaign optimisation, audience testing and performance reporting.
tools.training_notes: Master conversion tracking and consent mode before automation, guardrails (brand and location controls, text guidelines, negatives, URL exclusions), reading AI Max and PMax reports, learning-phase patience, reviewing Ask Advisor recommendations before approval, and ad policy. Advanced 14-20 hours.
tools.caveats: Forced migrations remove manual levers (DSA, language targeting, lookalike boundaries); generated copy needs brand and legal review and liability stays with the advertiser; performance claims are Google internal data; AI Mode shopping visibility is low; learning phases need 50-100 conversions; agentic changes must be gated by approval workflows.

tools.name: Meta Advantage+
tools.vendor: Meta Platforms, Inc. (Meta for Business, Ads Manager and Marketing API). Brief guess correct. Suite includes Advantage+ sales, app and leads campaigns, Advantage+ audience, placements, campaign budget, creative and catalog ads; legacy Advantage+ Shopping (ASC) and App (AAC) campaigns are being folded into the unified Advantage+ structure.
tools.what_it_is: Meta's AI automation layer inside Ads Manager and the Marketing API that lets the delivery system choose audiences, placements, budget allocation and creative variations across Facebook, Instagram, Messenger, Threads and Audience Network. Since February 2026 it is the default path in a single unified campaign-creation flow, and Meta's stated goal is fully automated campaigns from a URL and budget by end of 2026.
key_capabilities: Advantage+ sales, app and leads campaigns with budget liquidity in one campaign and up to 150 creative combinations
Advantage+ audience treats targeting inputs as suggestions rather than constraints
Advantage+ creative enhancements including generative backgrounds, image expansion, text variations, Image-to-Video, Brand Memory and Muse Image (Jul 2026)
Advantage+ campaign budget auto-allocation; existing-customer budget percentage cap
Creative Diversity Score and Customer Lifecycle (new-customer-only) toggle (2026)
Meta AI connected to ad accounts for analysis and reporting; Muse agent for small businesses linking Shopify, Klaviyo and Canva (Sep 2026)
tools.enterprise_data_handling: One set of terms for all advertisers. Business Tools Terms: pixel and Conversions API event data is used for ad delivery, measurement and to improve and personalise Meta products, retained up to two years; advertisers warrant notice and consent and must not send sensitive or children's data. Meta's generative-AI privacy page confirms Meta uses user information for generative AI but the opened page gives no advertiser-specific detail or business opt-out. Updated ad terms (effective 20 Nov 2026) make advertisers legally responsible for AI-generated content. No product-level SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA or FedRAMP attestations were available on pages that could be opened without login; controls are Business Manager roles, two-factor authentication and partner permissions.
tools.licensing_pricing: No licence or subscription; Ads Manager is free and costs are auction media spend. Marketing API docs: Meta computes an effective bid from bid strategy, bid amount and conversion probability, and "actual cost per result is usually around or less than bid_amount". Advantage+ and generative creative tools are included. Meta's public pricing and Business Help pages redirect to login and could not be opened.
tools.integrations: Conversions API and Meta Pixel, product catalogs, Marketing API v25, Meta Business Suite, Shopify, Klaviyo and Canva (Muse for SMB), HubSpot and Salesforce ad connectors, Sierra/Stripe/Walmart via the Personal Agent Protocol (Oct 2026).
tools.recent_developments: Feb 2025: streamlined Advantage+ sales, app and leads campaigns with audience, placements and budget on by default. Jun 2025: WSJ report of fully automated ads by end-2026. Oct 2025 (API v24): no new ASC/AAC via legacy API. 18 Feb 2026 (API v25): ASC/AAC creation and updates deprecated, remaining campaigns to be paused around v26 (Sep 2026); unified Ads Manager flow. Jun 2026 Cannes: end-to-end AI creative suite. Jul 2026: Muse Image in Advantage+ creative. Aug 2026: ad-set placement exclusions removed. Oct 2026: Threads a default placement.
tools.best_fit_departments: 32 Digital & Performance Marketing (Advanced): direct fit for campaign optimisation, audience testing and performance reporting.
tools.training_notes: Master Conversions API and pixel setup with consent, how to override Advantage+ defaults (age minimum, geo exclusions, excluded audiences), creative diversity requirements, incremental attribution, brand-safety review of generated assets and the new liability terms. Advanced 12-16 hours.
tools.caveats: Steady loss of placement and targeting control; learning phases need 50-100 conversions; AI-generated landing pages can bypass pixels and GA4; manual campaigns need migration before legacy APIs pause; metrics are Meta self-reported; official help and pricing pages are login-gated so verify terms in Ads Manager directly.
